subject: Re: Performance SLOs - p95/p99 latency (hosted vs current provider) - Finlytics
messages:
From: Sarah Cho <sarah@finlytics.io>
To: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Performance SLOs - p95/p99 latency (hosted vs current provider)

Hi Evelyn / Laura / Marissa,

Thanks again for the call today — good discussion. Per our notes, I wanted to capture the high-level SLO requirements and confirm next steps: 

- Primary target: end-to-end p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300ms (includes client-network + edge + service time).
- Expected sustained throughput: ~500 requests/sec during peak window (~3 hour burst), baseline 150 req/sec.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent users ~50; we may have short spikes to 150.
- Streaming: required for partial response token streaming to the client (we rely on early partial tokens for UX).
- Model footprint: currently using a 13B model hosted by our provider; very few model-side customizations.

Current provider observed tails: p95 ~150-220ms, p99 ~400-650ms end-to-end. We'd like to validate whether Redwood hosted API (or Dedicated) can reliably meet our p95/p99 targets under a realistic traffic profile.

Next steps we discussed:
1) Redwood to propose a simple test plan + measurement points (client vs edge vs post-LB).
2) Redwood to share benchmark results from a similar customer workload and suggested config (batching, concurrency knobs, streaming setup).
3) Schedule an engineering workshop to run a quick validation with real traffic and a short test account/credentials.

I've attached a CSV with our sample traffic profile (latency_test_plan.csv) and pasted the measurement points we'd prefer to use.

Thanks,

Sarah Cho
Head of Platform Engineering
Finlytics

Attachments: latency_test_plan.csv

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-15T18:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs - p95/p99 latency (hosted vs current provider)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear recap and the traffic profile. Quick confirmation items from our side before the workshop: 

- Measurement point: do you want SLOs measured at the client (browser/app) or at our edge (post-LB)? Client-side includes additional network variability; post-LB isolates service latency. Our recommendation is to agree on both: post-LB for service guarantees and client-side for UX impact.
- Do you have TLS termination at your edge or do we terminate? This affects e2e numbers slightly.
- Streaming: Redwood hosted supports chunked streaming with low tail latency; we'll include an example streaming config in the runbook.

I'll loop in Laura and Marissa for the benchmark numbers and a short testing runbook. Proposed next steps:
1) Engineering workshop: suggested slots Dec 21 or Dec 22 (engineering + infra + app eng).
2) We will provide a one-week test account with rate limits aligned to your peak profile and a small dataset to avoid cold-start variability.
3) We'll run two benchmark passes: baseline (no caching/batching) and optimized (with prefix cache + batching + streaming).

Attaching our SLO playbook and an outline of the runbook.

Best,

Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_slo_playbook.pdf

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Cho <sarah@finlytics.io>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-16T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs - p95/p99 latency (hosted vs current provider)

Sarah — adding some concrete numbers from our internal runs on similar 13B models and traffic shapes: 

- Redwood hosted (recommended config: streaming enabled, prefix caching, dynamic batching):
  - p95 (end-to-end, post-LB): 80-110 ms
  - p99 (end-to-end, post-LB): 180-260 ms
  - Notes: these runs used 50 concurrent connections with sustained 400 req/s and 4x short spikes.

- Typical current-provider numbers we've seen with similar setups:
  - p95: 150-220 ms
  - p99: 400-650 ms
  - Notes: higher tails driven by less aggressive KV-cache and larger batching tails.

Mitigations & knobs we'll test during the optimized pass:
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (expected 20-40% token compute reduction for hot paths).
- Dynamic batching policy tuned for your latency SLO (max batch window 5ms for low-latency use-case).
- Autoscaling warm pools for concurrency spikes to avoid cold-start tails.
- Streaming chunk size tuning to reduce first-byte latency while preserving throughput.

I attached the raw latency test CSV from our lab runs so you can eyeball distributions. We'll include the exact runner configs in the workshop.

-Laura
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: latency_test_results.csv
